title: 'We are devastated': Brampton man in mental health crisis dies after Peel police respond to 911 call for help
article: Several days after Michelle Campbell's brother died in the presence of Peel police, the family still didn't know where his body was being held.
"We are devastated. We can't get any answers. We have no idea where he is," she said, during a phone call on April 5.
Peter Campbell, 34, died after Peel Regional Police responded to a disturbance call at an apartment building near Kennedy Road and Vodden Street in Brampton on April 2.
Michelle said her other brother, Jason, had called 911 around 3 a.m. for an ambulance because Peter, who had schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, was having a mental health episode.
She noted Jason didn't want to call police, because Peter had ended up in hospital for two weeks after police were called last February under similar circumstances.
But it was police who responded to this call again.

According to a media release from the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), on April 2, Peel officers became involved in an interaction with a man at an apartment at Kennedy Road and Vodden Street in Brampton. The man was apprehended under the mental health act, the release said.
The SIU is an independent government agency that investigates police conduct that may have resulted in death or serious injury.
Shortly after being taken into custody, the man went into distress and then went vital signs absent, according to the SIU.
The officers administered first aid until paramedics arrived. The man was taken to hospital, where he was pronounced dead, the release said.
SIU said three investigators and two forensic investigators have been assigned to the death inquiry.
According to the family, the SIU is also investigating an earlier interaction with Peel police on Feb. 9, when Peter ended up in hospital with serious injuries.
Monica Hudon, spokesperson with the SIU, didn't confirm the two cases are connected.
"As the SIU does not identify complainants in our investigations, I'm not in a position to confirm any connection between the two cases," she explained.
She said Peel police responded to a call in Brampton on Feb. 8, shortly before midnight.
When officers entered the home, they became involved in an interaction with a 34-year-old man, she said.
The man was apprehended and taken to hospital by EMS for treatment of serious injuries, she explained.
Hudon said three investigators and one forensic investigator have been assigned to that case. As well, one subject official and eight witness officials have been designated.
Michelle said she had called 911 in the February incident because her brother was "acting strangely."
"I've never seen him like that," she explained.
She said she told the dispatcher her brother was having a mental health crisis.
Peel Regional Police Const. Tyler Bell-Morena said since the SIU has invoked its mandate, police cannot comment on either incident until after the findings of the SIU have been released.
That includes confirming if a mental health crisis support worker responded to either of the calls.
Bell-Morena is a former member of Peel's specialized mobile crisis rapid response team, which was set up specifically to assist with mental health crisis calls.
A specially trained uniformed officer along with a crisis support worker respond to emergency calls where there is a mental health concern or a crisis in progress.
Peel has three of the specialized units along with another unit that includes a single officer, available between the hours of 9 a.m. to midnight.

"When they are available, they are the primary response unit to all emergent mental health and addiction crisis calls in the region of Peel," he explained. "If they are busy on calls and unable to respond, then patrol officers will attend and liaise with (the unit)."
Michelle said when police showed up in February, her brother was throwing things around the apartment. She said he wasn't aiming at anyone.
She said she watched police "taser him over and over."
Police charged Peter with assault against a peace officer, resisting arrest and weapons dangerous.
His defence lawyer, Michael Moon, said all the charges were dropped near the end of March.
According to court documents, on March 27, the crown told the court it would not be in public interest to continue prosecution.
Moon said since the charges were withdrawn before any disclosure was shared, the defence wasn't permitted to view police bodycam footage.
Moon also said Peter was considering a civil case against police, pending the outcome of the SIU investigation.
Michelle said when police showed up on April 2, the family wasn't allowed in the apartment.
"They wouldn't let us go up. It was over an hour, and we have no idea what went on," she said.
Peter was taken by ambulance to hospital, but the family wasn't told where he was going, she said.
She said when new officers showed up on the scene and the original ones left, the family was told her brother had died.
The SIU is urging anyone who may have information about the investigation, including video or photos, to contact the lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529 or online at: https://siu.on.ca/en/appeals.php
Michelle said she can't understand why this happened, but the family wants answers.
"He just needed help. But no one would help him," she said.
The family started an online fundraising campaign through GoFundMe to raise money for Peter's funeral costs.
